newsitem.title: BELGIUM: ALL EU BANKS CAN BECOME BELGIAN PRIMARY DEALER.
newsitem.headline: ALL EU BANKS CAN BECOME BELGIAN PRIMARY DEALER.

text.p: All banks established in European Union member states will have the possibility to become primary dealers of Belgian state debt as of May 1, the Belgian Treasury said in a statement on Thursday.
The statement said the decision had been taken at a meeting on Wednesday between the Treasury, the central bank and the 15 existing primary dealers.

The primary dealers' rule book will be adapted to the European Investment Services Directive, which allows banks and brokerages authorised on their domestic markets to offer financial services in other EU states.
The ISD came into force in January 1996.
The statement said that central bank clearing services would be open to EU financial institutions.
The statement reiterated primary dealers were obliged to trade state debt on the regulated Belgian off-bourse market, using central bank clearing services.
"These measures prepare for the statute of euro primary dealer ahead of the monetary union from January 1, 1999," the Treasury said.
Current primary dealer regulations state that dealers have to be based in Belgium or Luxembourg.
In January the Brussels branch of Deutsche Bank AG , one of the current 15 primary dealers, moved most of its linear bond (OLO) trading activity from Brussels to London.
The move has sparked calls to adjust the rule-book and allow other foreign-based banks to operate as primary dealers.

Dealers said the Treasury had received several requests from foreign banks to become primary dealers in the run-up to a single currency union in 1999, provided they were allowed to operate from London.

The primary dealer system, set up in 1991, requires selected dealers to make a market in OLOs by continuously quoting bid and ask prices. They are allowed to take part in the Treasury's non-competitive OLO and Treasury bill auctions and enjoy a preferential relationship with the central bank.
